actions.task: Create the release keystore
actions.why: Play only accepts builds signed with your upload key; the project never stores a keystore.
actions.how:
1. keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore release.jks -alias upload -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -validity 10000
2. Store release.jks and both passwords in your password manager (losing them blocks future updates).
3. Enrol in Play App Signing when creating the app (STORE-2).
actions.verify: KEYSTORE_PATH=… ./gradlew :app:bundleProdRelease, then: apksigner verify --print-certs on an APK from the bundle

actions.task: Add the signing secrets to GitHub
actions.why: The release workflow (release-artifact.yml or release-play.yml) and the test-build workflows sign only when these secrets exist (HARD-07).
actions.how:
GitHub → repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret:
KEYSTORE_BASE64 = output of: base64 -i release.jks
KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, KEY_ALIAS, KEY_PASSWORD
actions.verify: Push a v* tag → the Release workflow uploads release-aab

actions.task: Add NVD_API_KEY for the dependency scan
actions.why: dependency-scan.yml (OWASP) fails or is extremely slow without an NVD API key (HARD-08).
actions.how:
1. Request a free key at https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/request-an-api-key
2. Add it as the GitHub secret NVD_API_KEY.
actions.verify: Actions → Dependency scan → Run workflow succeeds

actions.task: Protect main and require the CI check
actions.why: The rules are only enforced for humans if a red CI blocks merging (CI-01).
actions.how: GitHub → Settings → Branches → Add rule for main: require a pull request, require status check 'verify' (CI workflow), block force-pushes.
actions.verify: Open a PR with a failing test → merge is blocked

actions.task: Replace the placeholder app icon
actions.why: The template ships a placeholder launcher glyph.
actions.how: Android Studio → New → Image Asset (adaptive + monochrome) → replace app/src/main/res/drawable/ic_launcher_foreground.xml and the ic_launcher_background color.
actions.verify: Install the app: the launcher shows the real icon (also in themed-icons mode)

actions.task: Create the Play Console app and store listing
actions.why: Needed before the first upload: listing, content rating, target audience, privacy policy URL.
actions.how: Play Console → Create app (package {package}) → Store listing, App content (content rating, target audience, privacy policy, ads), enable Play App Signing.
actions.verify: Upload the AAB to the internal testing track without errors

actions.task: Fill in the Data safety form
actions.why: Required by Play; must list what the app and its SDKs collect ({sdk_list}).
actions.how: Play Console → App content → Data safety. Use each SDK's data-safety guidance; declare encryption in transit (HTTPS only).
actions.verify: Data safety section shows 'Completed'

actions.task: Set the release version
actions.why: versionCode must grow with every upload; the build reads it from Gradle properties.
actions.how: CI or local: ./gradlew :app:bundleProdRelease -Papp.versionCode=<n> -Papp.versionName=<x.y.z>
actions.verify: aapt2 dump badging shows the expected versionCode

actions.task: Confirm the production and stage API URLs
actions.why: Each flavor reads api.<flavor>.baseUrl; the skill only knew the URL given in intake.
actions.how: Set api.prod.baseUrl / api.stage.baseUrl in gradle.properties (or ~/.gradle/gradle.properties / CI -P). Include the API version in the path (DATA-07).
actions.verify: installStageDebug and installProdDebug both load data

actions.task: Confirm the certificate pins for the production host
actions.why: Wrong pins block every request in release builds; the skill read them from the live chain (HARD-01).
actions.how:
1. Compare api.prod.certPins with the commands in SPEC.md → Hardening (intermediate + root + backup roots).
2. Put a calendar reminder before the intermediate certificate expires.
actions.verify: Release build loads data; a pin mismatch shows an error, not 'no internet'

actions.task: Provide the stage environment
actions.why: The stage flavor ({stage_package}) talks to api.stage.baseUrl and installs next to prod.
actions.how: Make sure the stage backend exists and set api.stage.baseUrl / api.stage.certPins. Register {stage_package} wherever the prod package is registered (Firebase, deep links, OAuth).
actions.verify: installStageDebug shows 'Stage' in the app name and loads data

actions.task: Create the Firebase project and both Android apps
actions.why: Analytics, Crashlytics, push, Remote Config and App Distribution need a Firebase project.
actions.how: Firebase console → Add project → Add Android app twice: {package} and {stage_package} (or one project per environment). Add the SHA-1/SHA-256 of the debug and release/upload keys.
actions.verify: Both apps appear in Project settings

actions.task: Replace the placeholder google-services.json
actions.why: The skill used a placeholder so the build works; real Firebase services need the real file with both clients.
actions.how: Project settings → Your apps → download google-services.json (it contains both apps) → app/google-services.json. Keep it out of git if the team prefers (CI: store it as a secret and write it in the workflow).
actions.verify: App starts and Firebase logs show the project id; handover_check.py marks this Done

actions.task: Enable Crashlytics and test it
actions.why: Crash reports reach the dashboard only after the first crash from a configured app.
actions.how: Firebase → Crashlytics → Enable. Trigger a test crash from a debug-only menu, restart the app.
actions.verify: The test crash appears in Crashlytics

actions.task: Set up the backend sender
actions.why: The app only receives; something must send FCM messages (HTTP v1 API).
actions.how: Create a service account with the 'Firebase Cloud Messaging API Admin' role; send messages with notification.title/body and data.deeplink (allowed schemes only, PUSH-02).
actions.verify: Firebase console → Messaging → Send test message to a device token

actions.task: Bind PushTokenSink to the backend
actions.why: Until a PushTokenSink is bound, device tokens are not sent anywhere (PUSH-03).
actions.how: Implement PushTokenSink in :core:data (register the token through WorkManager with retry) and @Binds it; add the backend endpoint.
actions.verify: Fresh install → backend receives the token

actions.task: Create the Remote Config keys
actions.why: The app gate reads min_version_code (number) and maintenance_mode (boolean); missing keys fall back to the in-app defaults.
actions.how: Firebase → Remote Config → add min_version_code = 0 and maintenance_mode = false → Publish. Use conditions per app id for stage.
actions.verify: Set maintenance_mode=true → the app shows the maintenance screen after the next fetch

actions.task: Set up Firebase App Distribution for CI
actions.why: distribute-firebase.yml uploads the stage release build to testers with a service account.
actions.how:
1. Google Cloud console (the Firebase project) → IAM → service account with the role 'Firebase App Distribution Admin' → JSON key → GitHub secret FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON.
2. Firebase console → App Distribution → Testers & Groups → group 'testers' with the testers' emails.
actions.verify: Push to main (or run the workflow by hand) → testers get an email with the new build

actions.task: Add the Firebase app id for App Distribution
actions.why: The upload fails with 'Missing app id' until gradle.properties has it (it is not a secret).
actions.how: Firebase console → Project settings → Your apps → the Android app {stage_package} (single environment: {package}) → App ID (1:…:android:…) → gradle.properties: firebase.stage.appId= (single environment: firebase.appId=).
actions.verify: python3 tools/handover_check.py shows this item as Done

actions.task: Upload the first AAB to Play Console by hand
actions.why: The Play Developer API can't create an app or its first release; CI uploads work only after one manual upload.
actions.how: Play Console → Create app ({application_id}) → Testing → Internal testing → Create release → upload the signed AAB from tools/export_build.sh --type aab (or the CI artifact).
actions.verify: The internal release shows the build

actions.task: Enrol in Play App Signing with the upload key
actions.why: CI signs with the upload key (KEYSTORE_* secrets); Google re-signs with the app signing key.
actions.how: Play Console → Test and release → App integrity → App signing: let Google manage the app signing key; the upload key certificate must be the one in KEYSTORE_BASE64.
actions.verify: App integrity shows the upload key's SHA-256 = keytool -list -v -keystore <upload.jks>

actions.task: Give CI access to Play Console
actions.why: Gradle Play Publisher authenticates with a service account (ANDROID_PUBLISHER_CREDENTIALS).
actions.how:
1. Google Cloud console → enable 'Google Play Android Developer API' → service account → JSON key.
2. Play Console → Users and permissions → Invite the service account's email → app {application_id} → 'Release to testing tracks' (+ 'Release to production' for promote).
3. GitHub secret PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON = the JSON key.
actions.verify: Run the Play workflow by hand → a new internal release appears

actions.task: Protect the production environment
actions.why: promote-play.yml is the only way to production (CI-06); a required reviewer stops one person shipping alone.
actions.how: GitHub → Settings → Environments → New environment 'production' → Required reviewers (and Deployment branches/tags: v*). GitLab: Settings → CI/CD → Protected environments.
actions.verify: Running 'Promote to production' waits for an approval

actions.task: Back up the local upload keystore
actions.why: tools/export_build.sh --create-keystore keeps the key in ~/.android-keystores and its passwords in ~/.gradle/gradle.properties — outside the repo. Losing it blocks app updates.
actions.how: Copy ~/.android-keystores/<project>.jks and the <project>.keystore.* lines from ~/.gradle/gradle.properties into the team's password manager. For CI, base64 it into KEYSTORE_BASE64 with the same passwords.
actions.verify: The backup restores and tools/export_build.sh signs with it

actions.task: Choose how builds are delivered
actions.why: Intake answer was 'Decide later': the PR gate, the dependency scan and a signed AAB artifact on v* tags run; no build reaches testers.
actions.how: Pick local APK/AAB, Firebase App Distribution, Google Play internal testing and/or Google Play release, then ask Claude (android-engineer Task mode) to add the channel — it renders only that channel's workflow and wiring.
actions.verify: docs/SPEC.md 'Distribution:' lists the channels

actions.task: Publish assetlinks.json on every deep-link host
actions.why: https App Links open the app only after Android verifies the domain (autoVerify).
actions.how: Serve https://<host>/.well-known/assetlinks.json listing {package} (and {stage_package} on the stage host) with the SHA-256 of the Play App Signing key (Play Console → App integrity).
actions.verify: adb shell pm get-app-links {package} shows 'verified'

actions.task: Configure the login provider
actions.why: Sign-in needs the provider/console setup the app can't do (OAuth clients, SSO, OTP sender).
actions.how: Create OAuth/SSO clients for {package} and {stage_package} with the right SHA-1s; configure the OTP/SMS sender; document test accounts.
actions.verify: Sign in works on stage and prod builds

actions.task: Firebase Analytics: check events and conversions
actions.why: Events are sent once the real google-services.json is in place (FB-2).
actions.how: Firebase → Analytics → Events: mark key events as conversions; enable DebugView with adb shell setprop debug.firebase.analytics.app {package}.
actions.verify: DebugView shows the app's events

actions.task: Adjust: app token and event tokens
actions.why: Adjust stays off without the app token and only sends events that have a token (OBS-05).
actions.how: Adjust dashboard → create the app → set analytics.adjust.appToken and analytics.adjust.eventTokens=name:token,… in ~/.gradle/gradle.properties or CI.
actions.verify: Sandbox install appears in the Adjust testing console

actions.task: AppsFlyer: dev key
actions.why: AppsFlyer stays off without the dev key.
actions.how: AppsFlyer dashboard → App settings → Dev key → analytics.appsflyer.devKey.
actions.verify: SDK integration test in the AppsFlyer dashboard passes

actions.task: Mixpanel: project token
actions.why: Mixpanel stays off without the project token.
actions.how: Mixpanel → Project settings → Project token → analytics.mixpanel.token.
actions.verify: Events appear in Mixpanel → Events (live view)

actions.task: Amplitude: API key
actions.why: Amplitude stays off without the API key.
actions.how: Amplitude → Settings → Projects → API key → analytics.amplitude.apiKey.
actions.verify: Events appear in Amplitude → User lookup

actions.task: Segment: write key and destinations
actions.why: Segment stays off without the write key; it forwards only to destinations you enable.
actions.how: Segment → Sources → Android source → write key → analytics.segment.writeKey; enable destinations.
actions.verify: Source debugger shows the events

actions.task: {provider}: keys and dashboard
actions.why: The {provider} provider was written for a library the user named; it stays off until its keys are set.
actions.how: Create the app in the {provider} dashboard and set the keys read by {provider}AnalyticsProvider (see core/analytics/build.gradle.kts).
actions.verify: Events appear in the {provider} dashboard

actions.task: Decide on analytics consent
actions.why: The composite starts enabled; markets with opt-in rules (e.g. GDPR) need consent first.
actions.how: If opt-in is required: call analyticsTracker.setEnabled(false) at startup and true after consent; list the SDKs in the privacy policy.
actions.verify: With consent off, no provider dashboard receives events

actions.task: Replace the placeholder TV banner
actions.why: Google TV shows the 320 × 180 banner in the app row; Play rejects TV apps without a real one (TVM-01).
actions.how:
1. Export a 320 × 180 px banner with the app name in the image, no transparency.
2. Replace app-tv/src/main/res/drawable/tv_banner.xml (or add drawable-xhdpi/tv_banner.png and delete the XML).
actions.verify: Install the TV build on a Google TV emulator: the app row shows the new banner

actions.task: Opt in to Android TV and create the Android TV release track
actions.why: The TV bundle is a separate upload to the same app (same applicationId) on its own release track (TVM-02).
actions.how:
Play Console → your app → Test and release → Advanced settings → Form factors → + Add form factor → Android TV.
Then create a release on the Android TV track with the bundle from ./gradlew :app-tv:bundleProdRelease.
actions.verify: Play Console shows the Android TV track with the TV bundle

actions.task: Add the TV store listing assets
actions.why: TV listings need TV screenshots and the banner; phone screenshots are not accepted for TV.
actions.how: Play Console → Store presence → Main store listing → Android TV: at least one 1920 × 1080 screenshot (Home, a list, detail, player) and the TV banner.
actions.verify: The listing preview shows the TV section

actions.task: Keep the TV version codes above the phone's
actions.why: Two bundles of one app must never share a versionCode (TVM-02).
actions.how: app.versionCode in gradle.properties is the phone's; the TV build adds 1,000,000. Bump app.versionCode once per release for both.
actions.verify: ./gradlew :app-tv:assembleProdRelease and check the APK's versionCode with apkanalyzer manifest version-code

actions.task: Test on a real TV with its remote
actions.why: Emulators don't show remote quirks (long-press, media keys, slow CPUs) or overscan on real panels.
actions.how: Install the stage build on a Google TV device (adb connect <tv-ip>): walk every screen with the remote only, check the focus maps in SPEC.md, the Back chain, playback keys and holding ↓ on the longest list.
actions.verify: Every focus map in SPEC.md behaves on the device

actions.task: Add large-screen screenshots and check large-screen quality
actions.why: Tablets get their own screenshots in the listing, and Play ranks apps by its large-screen quality checks.
actions.how: Play Console → Store listing: 7-inch and 10-inch tablet screenshots (expanded layout). Then Play Console → Quality → Android vitals / large screens: fix any reported issue.
actions.verify: Tablet screenshots appear in the listing preview

actions.task: Use the old app's release (upload) key — do NOT create a new one
actions.why: The rebuild must update the installed app in place: a different key can't update installed copies, and Play rejects it for the existing listing.
actions.how:
1. Get the old app's release/upload keystore and passwords from wherever the last release was signed.
2. Put them in CI secrets (SIGN-2) and your password manager.
3. With Play App Signing, this is the upload key: compare its SHA-256 with Play Console → App integrity.
actions.verify: apksigner verify --print-certs on the new APK and on the Play-installed old APK: same SHA-256 digest

actions.task: Release as an update of the existing Play listing ({application_id}), not a new app
actions.why: Same applicationId keeps users, ratings and installs; the versionCode must be above the last release (MIG-01).
actions.how: Upload the bundle to the existing app in Play Console; release notes list the visible changes (SPEC.md Deviations).
actions.verify: Play Console accepts the bundle for {application_id} with the new versionCode

actions.task: Staged rollout 10 % → 50 % → 100 % with crash-free monitoring
actions.why: The update migrates every user's database and settings once; a migration bug hits real data.
actions.how:
1. Internal testing track first, installed over a Play-installed old version.
2. Production at 10 %; watch crash-free users and ANRs (Android vitals or the crash reporter) for 2–3 days.
3. 50 %, then 100 %. Halt the rollout on any crash in the database/DataStore startup path.
actions.verify: Rollout history shows the steps; crash-free rate at least the old release's

actions.task: Plan the rollback: the data migration is one-way
actions.why: Play can't install a lower versionCode, so a rollback is the old code re-released with a higher one — and the old SQLiteOpenHelper crashes on the newer database ('Can't downgrade database'); SharedPreferencesMigration already deleted the old prefs file.
actions.how: Prefer halting the staged rollout and shipping a forward fix. If a rollback build is needed: old code + onDowngrade that rebuilds the old tables from the new ones (ids kept, old user_version) + default prefs, versionCode above the bad release.
actions.verify: Install the rollback build over the new release on an emulator with data: no crash, data kept

actions.task: Run the upgrade test on real devices from Play-installed builds
actions.why: The emulator runs used re-signed APKs; real installs may carry older versions and real backups.
actions.how: tools/migration/upgrade_test.sh with the old APK from Play (App bundle explorer) and the oldest version still installed (Play stats → versions); also restore an Auto Backup made by the old app onto a fresh install of the new one.
actions.verify: All checks PASS (docs/migration/parity.md)

actions.task: Confirm the deviations from the old app
actions.why: SPEC.md lists every intended change: fixed quirks, new or removed behaviour, look changes.
actions.how: Review docs/SPEC.md 'Deviations' and docs/migration/parity.md; record the sign-off in SPEC.md.
actions.verify: Sign-off in SPEC.md

actions.task: Check the Data safety form against the old answers
actions.why: New SDKs or permissions change the answers; an unchanged data model doesn't.
actions.how: Compare the new manifest permissions and SDK list ({sdk_list}) with the old release's form.
actions.verify: Data safety form updated or confirmed
